# Plan: Add saved project views

## Review request
Review this plan directly; skip optional /office-hours.
After I select a review mode, briefly explain in your own words how you will
apply that mode to this plan before asking the next review question.

## Goal
Team members repeatedly recreate filters on a project task list. Let each
member save a named combination of filters and sort order and reopen it later.

## Approach
- Add a saved_views table scoped to the project and member.
- Provide authenticated create, list, update, and delete endpoints.
- Add a view picker and a save action beside the existing task filters.
- Keep existing task access rules when applying a saved view.

## Validation
- Test persistence, project access, and reopening a view after task changes.
- Measure whether members reuse saved views during a two-week pilot.

D1 — Add gstack skill routing rules to CLAUDE.md?
Project/branch/task: plan-review fixture on `main`, reviewing PLAN.md (saved project views).
ELI10: gstack skills work best when the project's CLAUDE.md tells Claude which skill to reach for (bugs → /investigate, scope → /plan-ceo-review, etc.). This is a one-time setup prompt, separate from the plan review itself. Plan mode is active, so if you say yes the CLAUDE.md edit and commit happen after the review ends, not now.
Stakes if we pick wrong: Without routing, skills only run when you type them by hand; with it, a few extra lines land in CLAUDE.md.
Recommendation: A because routing rules are cheap and make future sessions pick the right skill without prompting.
Note: options differ in kind, not coverage — no completeness score.
Net: a few lines of CLAUDE.md config vs. invoking skills manually forever.

options.label: Add routing rules (recommended)
options.description:
✅ Future requests auto-route to the right gstack skill without you naming it
✅ One short section appended to CLAUDE.md, committed once, easy to remove later
❌ Edit is deferred until plan mode exits; adds ~15 lines to the project instructions file

options.label: No thanks, manual only
options.description:
✅ CLAUDE.md stays exactly as it is; nothing extra committed to the fixture repo
✅ You keep full control over when each skill runs by typing /skill-name yourself
❌ Skills never trigger from natural-language requests; this prompt will not reappear for this project

questions.question:
D2 — M1: Which review mode should govern this plan?
Project/branch/task: `main`, reviewing PLAN.md "Add saved project views" (fixture repo, plan only).
ELI10: The mode sets my posture for the rest of the review. Expansion means I pitch bigger versions and adjacent wins; Selective means I harden what you have and offer expansions neutrally one at a time; Hold means I keep scope frozen and go deep on failure paths and tests; Reduction means I look for what to cut. Every scope change still needs your yes regardless of mode.
Stakes if we pick wrong: Too ambitious and a 1-day feature turns into a platform project; too narrow and the schema locks in per-member-only views that need a migration when the team asks to share them.
Recommendation: SELECTIVE EXPANSION because this is an added capability in an existing system (~9-12 files), and there are exactly two or three expansions worth weighing (shared views, deep-link URLs, a defined pilot metric) without rewriting the plan.
Note: options differ in kind, not coverage — no completeness score.
Net: how hard I push on ambition vs. rigor for the next ten sections.

options.label: SELECTIVE EXPANSION (recommended)
options.description:
✅ Hardens the current four bullets first (failure paths, tests, access rules), then offers each expansion neutrally with effort and risk
✅ Fits an enhancement to an existing system: you cherry-pick shared views, deep links, or metrics without a scope avalanche
❌ Each expansion is a separate question, so more decisions land on you than in Hold Scope

options.label: SCOPE EXPANSION
options.description:
✅ I pitch the platonic ideal: shared team views, default views, deep links, templates, delight items, argued enthusiastically
✅ Best if you want this to become the team's triage layer rather than a personal bookmark
❌ Turns a ~1 hour CC feature into a multi-part project; easy to over-build before the pilot proves reuse

options.label: HOLD SCOPE
options.description:
✅ Maximum rigor on exactly the four bullets: error map, edge cases, race conditions, test diagram, observability
✅ Fastest path to a shippable pilot with the smallest diff
❌ Shared views and linkable URLs are not offered; if the schema is per-member-only it costs a migration later

options.label: SCOPE REDUCTION
options.description:
✅ Strips to the minimum viable core (maybe just save + reopen, no update endpoint) to test demand fastest
✅ Lowest risk if you doubt the pain is real
❌ The plan is already small (~9-12 files); cutting further mostly removes tests and edge handling, which cost seconds with CC

questions.question:
D3 — R3: How should "members reuse saved views" be defined and measured for the two-week pilot?
Project/branch/task: `main`, PLAN.md "Add saved project views", HOLD SCOPE review.
ELI10: The plan promises to measure reuse in a two-week pilot, but never says what reuse means or how it gets counted. Right now nothing in the plan records that a view was opened, so at day 14 there is no number to read. This decision picks the definition and the smallest way to record it. It does not add features; it makes an acceptance criterion the plan already states actually checkable.
Stakes if we pick wrong: Pick nothing and the pilot ends with anecdotes; pick counters and you can say "3 opens" but not whether that was one Monday burst or steady use across days.
Recommendation: A because per-day reuse is the question the pilot is asking, events are the standard way to answer it, and the code is ~30 lines (human: ~half a day / CC: ~10 min).
Completeness: A=10/10, B=6/10, C=3/10
Net: a real answer at day 14 vs. a counter that can't tell habit from a burst vs. asking people to remember.

options.label: Events + per-day definition (recommended)
options.description: Emit created/applied/deleted events for saved views through the existing analytics path and define reuse as a view applied on 2+ distinct days after creation. Effort S. Risk low. Reuse: existing event/analytics pipeline (verify). Verification: unit tests that apply emits one event, denied apply emits none. ✅ Answers the actual pilot question: are people coming back to a view on different days ✅ No writes on the saved_views row during reads, so applying a view stays a pure read path ❌ Depends on an analytics/event path existing; if none, a small events table is added (still S)

options.label: Counters on the row
options.description: Add open_count and last_applied_at columns to saved_views and bump them on apply; reuse = open_count >= 3 by pilot end. Effort S. Risk low. Reuse: none beyond the new table. Verification: unit test that apply increments once and denied apply does not. ✅ Zero new infrastructure; a single SQL query at pilot end gives the number ✅ Trivial to implement and read, no pipeline to verify ❌ Cannot distinguish three opens in one minute from three separate days, and every apply becomes a write

options.label: End-of-pilot survey only
options.description: No instrumentation. Ask pilot members after two weeks whether they reused their saved views. Effort S (zero code). Risk medium. Reuse: n/a. Verification: none. ✅ No code, no schema, nothing to test or maintain ✅ Captures qualitative reasons a number never would ❌ Recall bias and self-selection; the plan's stated "measure" criterion is not actually met

questions.question:
D4 — R5: Keep the update endpoint (rename / overwrite a saved view) in this plan, or defer it?
Project/branch/task: gstack-plan-count-2n1ktg on main, PLAN.md "Add saved project views", HOLD SCOPE.
ELI10: The plan lists create, list, update, delete. Update is the only one the goal does not strictly need: during a two-week pilot a member can delete a view and save it again under a new name. Dropping it removes one endpoint, its authorization check, the rename control in the picker, and their tests. Keeping it means members can rename or "save changes" to a view in place, which is what every incumbent offers.
Stakes if we pick wrong: Defer and members hit a small annoyance (delete + re-save) and the pilot cannot tell "edited my view" from "gave up on it". Keep and you carry one more endpoint's error paths and tests; with CC that is minutes, not days.
Recommendation: B) Keep in scope because update is cheap with CC (human: ~half day / CC: ~10 min), users expect rename, and the HOLD posture prefers full coverage of the scope you already wrote.
Completeness: A=7/10, B=10/10.
Net: one fewer endpoint in the pilot vs. a complete CRUD surface with no re-create workaround.

options.label: A) Defer to TODOS.md
options.description:
Summary: Ship create/list/delete only; record update (rename/overwrite) in TODOS.md with the reason "not needed to reopen a view; revisit after pilot". Effort: S. Risk: low. Reuse: no new code. Verification coverage: none for update; existing tests for the other endpoints unchanged.
✅ Smallest API surface for the two-week pilot; one fewer authorization path to get wrong
✅ Delete + re-save covers rename during the pilot with no data loss
❌ Members cannot fix a typo or tweak a view in place; the pilot metric conflates "edited" with "abandoned"

options.label: B) Keep in scope (recommended)
options.description:
Summary: Keep PATCH/PUT update for name and filter/sort payload, owner-only, with rename and "save changes" controls in the picker. Effort: S. Risk: low. Reuse: same model validation and authorization policy as create/delete. Verification coverage: request tests (non-owner → 404, stale id → 404, name collision → 422, empty payload → 422) and model tests for validation.
✅ Members rename or adjust a view in place; matches Asana/Linear/Jira behavior they already know
✅ Full CRUD means the pilot's "reuse" metric reflects real use, not re-create churn
❌ One more endpoint whose error paths, authorization and tests must be traced in the review

# Plan: Add saved project views

## Review request
Review this plan directly; skip optional /office-hours.
After I select a review mode, briefly explain in your own words how you will
apply that mode to this plan before asking the next review question.

## Goal
Team members repeatedly recreate filters on a project task list. Let each
member save a named combination of filters and sort order and reopen it later.

## Approach
- Add a saved_views table scoped to the project and member.
- Provide authenticated create, list, update, and delete endpoints.
- Add a view picker and a save action beside the existing task filters.
- Keep existing task access rules when applying a saved view.

## Validation
- Test persistence, project access, and reopening a view after task changes.
- Measure whether members reuse saved views during a two-week pilot.
